title: Foundation
description: Levelling feet for a base: set it down on ground no steeper than ten degrees, found the base, and its jacks reach down to hold it level. A founded base cannot be pushed or tipped - though what hits it can still break it.

title: Base Core
description: The heart of a base: control, a little power in reserve and a few panels on the roof, room for four. Set it down on a foundation, found it, and build out from its connectors.

title: Habitat Module
description: Living space for six: bunks, galley, a window on the world outside. Brought in on a flatbed and joined at a connector.

title: Propellant Depot
description: Twelve tonnes of propellant in store: what a base fills its craft from, and what a tanker tops up.

title: Monopropellant Depot
description: Monopropellant for thrusters, kept in four spheres.

title: Power Module
description: Batteries racked floor to ceiling: what keeps a base's lamps lit and pumps running through the night.

title: Solar Array
description: Two wings of solar cells on a mast, for the top of a module. Power by day, none by night: a base wants batteries too.

title: Base Connector
description: A wide hatch for the side of a base module. Bring another module's connector up to it, near enough lined up, and they draw together and join into one base.

title: Corridor
description: A walkway between two modules. Put a connector on each end.

title: Pad Deck
description: A twelve-metre slab to launch from and land on. Founded on its own or joined to a base, it is a launch site: craft set down on it fill up from the base's stores, and a craft standing on it can be refuelled.

title: Floodlight Mast
description: A six-metre mast with a lamp head, lit at night while the base has power.

title: Flatbed
description: A long low deck on eight wheel mounts, for carrying a module: a cab at the front, a release clamp in the middle to hold the load and set it down.

title: Release Clamp
description: Holds a load on a flatbed. Stage it and it lets go, staying on the flatbed while the load drops free on its own feet.
